main_text.p: numero, una fit fpecie & eadem, neceffe eft. His philofophi verbis perfpicuum eft palin-genefiam, non novam effe mortuorum generationem, fed duntaxat factam in corporibus alterationem. Huc accedit quod generatione ἐντελέχεια corporis acquiritur[?]. At in palingenefia nulla corporis ἐντελέχεια acquiritur, fed duntaxat materiae, quae in universi elementis poteftate erat, forma animaque reftituitur. Nam morte & interitu hominis mentem extingui abolerique nemo eft qui fibi perfuadeat, nifi fumme fit impius & brutiffimus, quoniam mentis effentia incorporea eft & fimplex, nullisque corporeis affectionibus per fe obnoxia, ficuti non infcite philofophus, libro De anima tertio, perfpicue demonftrat. Id quod magis magif-que facrofanctae fcripturae teftimonio confirmari poteft. Ibi enim Deus Abrahami effe dicitur, & Ifachi, atque Jacobi. Sed (ut rectiffime nofter Christus affumit) Deus viuentium eft, non autem mortuorum. Itaque ipforum patrum animae ἐντελέχειαι quae non extinctae funt nec abolitae, fed ab ipfo Deo conferuatae, donec fua repetant priftina corpora, quae in inferiori vniuerfo delitescunt & confiftunt. Ex quibus perfpicuum eft palingenefiam non mutationem effe fub-ftantiae, fed qualitatis corporis humani, quam Apoftolus priore epiftola ad Corinthios ἀνάστασιν νεκρῶν appellat. Haec enim mortuo-

page.notes: The word "acquiritur" in the first full line of the main text is partly obscured by a dark mark over "corporis", so it is doubtful. The Greek words are copied as far as they can be read in the scan; the Greek phrase at the end of the page (ἀνάστασιν νεκρῶν) is less clear than the rest. The hyphenated line breaks "magif-que" and "fub-ftantiae" keep the printed hyphens. The page has no marginal notes or headings. The catchword "rum" is the first word of the next page.
